'''Tony Lee Bradley Jr.''' (born January 8, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|University of North Carolina]] (UNC). A {{height|ft=6|in=10}} [[center (basketball)|center]], Bradley was a primary substitute for the Tar Heels' [[2016–17 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2017 NCAA championship team]].

Bradley was selected by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with the 28th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]], but was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] on draft night. After three seasons with the Jazz, Bradley was ultimately traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2020 before being traded midseason to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the 2021 offseason and spent two seasons with the team. After a two-season stint in the [[NBA G League]], Bradley signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]], with whom he reached the [[2025 NBA Finals]].

==High school career==
Born and raised in [[Bartow, Florida]], Bradley played high school basketball for [[Bartow High School]]. He was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] in his senior year.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Tony Bradley restores the 'Tar Heel order' in the McDonald's All American Game|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/tony-bradley-restores-the-tar-heel-order-in-the-mcdonalds-all-american-game|work=[[USA Today]]|date=January 22, 2016|access-date=April 16, 2017}}</ref> Bradley chose North Carolina over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] and [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Reggie|last=Rankin|title=North Carolina opens 2016 class with five-star center Tony Bradley|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/13569012|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=September 3, 2015|access-date=April 16, 2017}}</ref> Bradley was rated as a five-star recruit and was ranked 17th in the ESPN 100 for the Class of 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tony Bradley – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/188096|website=ESPN.com|date=January 7, 2016|access-date=January 7, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Tony Bradley, 2016 Center|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/tony-bradley-464|website=Rivals.com|date=January 7, 2016|access-date=January 7, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season, Bradley served as the primary substitute for senior [[Kennedy Meeks]], averaging 7.5 points and 5.1 rebounds in 14.6 minutes per game and providing strong offensive rebounding for the Tar Heels.<ref>{{cite news|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|title=Tony Bradley is UNC's best pro prospect you haven't heard about — and he likes it that way|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/tony-bradley-unc-nba-draft-2017-north-carolina-basketball-final-four-scouting-report/5z6vdu1ac59b162nqyrovcxnv|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=April 1, 2017|access-date=April 16, 2017|archive-date=July 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180718001256/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/tony-bradley-unc-nba-draft-2017-north-carolina-basketball-final-four-scouting-report/5z6vdu1ac59b162nqyrovcxnv|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Following the Tar Heels' championship win over [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], Bradley announced that he would declare his eligibility for the [[2017 NBA draft]] without signing an agent, leaving open the opportunity to return to UNC for his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite news|title=UNC's Bradley to test NBA draft waters after title win|url=http://collegebasketball.ap.org/article/uncs-bradley-test-nba-draft-waters-after-title-win|agency=Associated Press|date=April 4, 2017|access-date=April 16, 2017}}</ref> Bradley ultimately chose to remain in the NBA draft, becoming the third "one-and-done" player during Williams' tenure at UNC and the second among those to have won a national championship.<ref>{{cite news|title=UNC Basketball: Tony Bradley Jr. to stay in NBA Draft|url=http://keepingitheel.com/2017/05/24/unc-basketball-tony-bradley-jr-stay-nba-draft/|work=Fansided|date=May 24, 2017|access-date=June 20, 2017|archive-date=September 2, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220902184806/http://keepingitheel.com/2017/05/24/unc-basketball-tony-bradley-jr-stay-nba-draft/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Utah Jazz (2017–2020)===
Bradley was selected 28th overall by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the 2017 NBA Draft with his draft rights traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] for [[Josh Hart]] (30th overall) and [[Thomas Bryant]] (42nd overall).<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Draft Rights to Tony Bradley from Los Angeles Lakers|url=https://www.nba.com/news/utah-jazz-acquire-draft-rights-tony-bradley-los-angeles-lakers|website=NBA.com|date=June 22, 2017|access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref> On July 5, 2017, Bradley signed with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jazz Sign 2017 Draft Pick Tony Bradley|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-2017-draft-pick-tony-bradley/|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2017|access-date=July 5, 2017}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on November 5 against the [[Houston Rockets]]. He was assigned to the Jazz's [[G League]] affiliate, the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] on November 7, and made his G League debut the next night, scoring 20 points in a loss to the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jazz Assign Bradley and O'Neale to Salt Lake City Stars|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-assign-bradley-and-oneale-salt-lake-city-stars|website=NBA.com|date=November 7, 2017|access-date=November 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dunigan's Clutch Buckets Lift Herd Over Stars|url=http://gleague.nba.com/games/20171108/WISSLC/|website=NBA.com|date=November 8, 2017|access-date=November 9, 2017}}</ref> Bradley made nine appearances for Utah during his rookie campaign, averaging 0.9 points, 1.2 rebounds and 0.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tony Bradley 2017-18 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065673/type/nba/year/2018|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

Bradley made only three appearances for the Jazz during the [[2018–19 NBA season]], averaging 5.7 points, 5.0 rebounds and 0.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tony Bradley 2018-19 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065673/type/nba/year/2019|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> He entered the rotation for the [[2019–20 NBA season]], playing in 58 total games (including three starts), in which he averaged 4.9 points, 4.6 rebounds and 0.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tony Bradley 2019-20 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065673/type/nba/year/2020|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2021)===
On November 22, 2020, Bradley and the draft rights to [[Saben Lee]] were traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Cash Considerations|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-cash-considerations|website=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2020|access-date=November 22, 2020}}</ref> A day later, Bradley was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Zhaire Smith]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Team Acquires Bradley|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-acquires-bradley|website=NBA.com|date=November 23, 2020|access-date=November 23, 2020}}</ref> He made 20 appearances (eight starts) for Philadelphia during the [[2020–21 NBA season]], averaging 5.5 points, 5.2 rebounds and 0.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tony Bradley 2020-21 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065673/type/nba/year/2021|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2021)===
On March 25, 2021, Bradley was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a three-way trade involving the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Tony Bradley, Austin Rivers, Two Second-Round Draft Picks and Generates Trade Exception|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions-210325|website=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> He made 22 appearances for the Thunder, averaging 8.7 points, 6.1 rebounds and 0.9 assists.

===Chicago Bulls (2021–2023)===
On August 19, 2021, Bradley signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bulls Sign Bradley, Green and Dotson|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agents-bradley-green-and-dotson|website=NBA.com|date=August 19, 2021|access-date=August 20, 2021}}</ref> He made 55 appearances (seven starts) for Chicago during the [[2021–22 NBA season]], averaging 3.0 points, 3.4 rebounds and 0.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tony Bradley 2021-22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065673/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

Bradley made 12 appearances for the Bulls in the [[2022–23 NBA season]], logging averages of 1.6 points, 0.9 rebounds and 0.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tony Bradley 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065673/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> On February 21, 2023, Bradley was waived by the Bulls.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Ben|last=Stinar|title=Chicago Bulls Will Reportedly Release This Player|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/chicago-bulls-will-reportedly-release-this-player-tony-bradley-nba-tuesday|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023}}</ref>

===Texas Legends (2023–2024)===
On October 20, 2023, Bradley signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks have signed Tony Bradley.|number=1715134833008259235|user=MavsPR|date=October 19, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> but was waived the same day.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks have waived Tony Bradley.|number=1715471157334245533|user=MavsPR|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> On October 29, he joined the G League's [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Britney|last=Wynn|title=LEGENDS DRAFT FOUR, FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-draft-four-finalize-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref>

===College Park Skyhawks (2024–2025)===
On October 7, 2024, Bradley signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]], but was waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Hawks Sign, Waive Tony Bradley|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/hawks-sign-center-tony-bradley.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 8, 2024|access-date=October 8, 2024}}</ref> On October 26, he joined the G League's [[College Park Skyhawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Finalize Training Camp Schedule and Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/college-park-skyhawks-finalize-training-camp-schedule-and-roster/n-6159937|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}}</ref>

=== Indiana Pacers (2025–2026) ===
On March 2, 2025, Bradley signed a 10-day contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indiana Pacers Sign Tony Bradley to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-sign-tony-bradley-to-10-day-contract |access-date=2025-03-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en|date=March 2, 2025}}</ref> On March 13, he signed a second 10-day contract with the team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pacers Sign Tony Bradley To Second 10-Day, Final Roster Spot Still Center|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tonyeast/2025/03/13/pacers-sign-tony-bradley-to-second-10-day-final-roster-spot-still-center/|access-date=April 4, 2025|website=forbes.com|language=en|date=March 13, 2025|last=East|first=Tony}}</ref> On March 23, the Pacers signed Bradley for the rest of the [[2024–25 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Pacers' Tony Bradley: Sticking around for rest of season | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-03-23 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-tony-bradley-sticking-around-for-rest-of-season/ | access-date=2025-12-03}}</ref> In 14 appearances for Indiana, he averaged 4.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 0.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tony Bradley 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065673/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> The Pacers, along with Bradley, would go on to make the [[2025 NBA Finals]], but they would lose in seven games by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].

On January 5, 2026, Bradley was waived by the Pacers,<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Transactions - Jan. 5, 2025|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-transactions-jan-5-2025|date=January 5, 2026|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 5, 2026}}</ref> but on January 8, he was re-signed to another 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Transactions - Jan. 8, 2025|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-transactions-jan-8-2026|date=January 8, 2026|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 8, 2026}}</ref> On January 19, Bradley re-signed with the Pacers on a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pacers' Tony Bradley: Signs another 10-day deal|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-tony-bradley-signs-another-10-day-deal/|access-date=February 2, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== Atlanta Hawks (2026) ===
On April 6, 2026, Bradley signed a rest-of-season contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Tony Bradley {{!}} Atlanta Hawks |url=https://hawks.com/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-tony-bradley |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=hawks.com |language=en}}</ref>
